text: Keep a server safe when anyone can create accounts and graphs: limits, no terminals, foreign text is data
description:
Felix 2026-11-10: write access must never allow spawning a terminal; "we have to make that very secure. And prompt injection is still a security issue we need to be aware of."

With open sign-up, automatic accounts and graphs created by strangers, a server needs:
- limits per account and per address: number of graphs, their size, notes and offers per hour
- a way for the server admin to remove graphs and accounts
- terminals and agents stay off for everyone except what the server admin switches on for themselves (as today: local-only routers, AIMPARENCY_AGENTS)
- text from notes, offers and other people's graphs reaches agents only as data, never as instructions
- reading from other origins allowed, writing only with the account's own proof of login, never through cookies a foreign page could use

Added 2026-11-12, because any account may add a repo by remote URL and keep SSH keys on the server (548c5b94):
- the server fetches addresses that strangers enter: only https and ssh, no addresses inside the server's own network, limits on size and time
- SSH keys on the server: usable only for the repos their account selected, never readable through the API, never used for another account
- nothing from a fetched repo is executed (no hooks, no submodules), as today

Builds on the audit of 2026-11-09 (bb34c22a), which covered one read-only graph per server.

status.comment:
2026-11-13 (93d46dce, e5d3bf4a, 9102def6, 32ba03c0). Built: limits for new accounts per address and hour, graphs per account, notes per account and hour, the size of a graph cloned from a URL; server admins remove graphs and accounts; agents, loops and server paths stay off with accounts, a token limited to graphs never reaches the agents gateway; notes reach agents only as marked visitors' text; other websites read and never write, also with a valid token; remote URLs are fetched only over https and ssh from public addresses, with git pinned to the checked address, no redirects, no hooks, and nothing of the server user's git setup; SSH keys are made on the server, usable only by their account for its graphs, and no procedure returns a private key. Evidence: auth/sign-up.test.ts, graphs/remote-graph.test.ts, auth/one-port-server.test.ts, guest/notes.test.ts.

2026-11-22: graph size limit for every space, not only cloned ones: with accounts, the access middleware (trpc.ts) measures a space's .bowman before each mutation (graphs/size-limit.ts; cache/ and runtime/ do not count) and refuses it with PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE past limits.graphMegabytes (default 50); delete…/remove… procedures stay allowed so a space can shrink again. Clone check uses the same module. Evidence: graphs/size-limit.test.ts (over the limit refused, delete allowed, fits again after), graphs/auth/guest/server tests 119/120 with the one failure a pre-existing parallel-load teardown race in remote-graph.test.ts (fails the same without this change), tsc clean.

Still open: limits for offers come with b7e0b972; a single request has no size bound of its own (idea text/description have no max, the WebSocket default max message is large), so one write can overshoot the limit once; git history (.git) is not counted; nothing here was tried against a running public server.
